page.layout: One printed page. Running head at top, page number at top left. One text column with a narrow margin on the left holding one note ("lin. 18."), beside the second paragraph.

main_text.p: مــا يريدن فالعدل ـــ وضع الشي في موضعه وهو التصرف في الملك علي مقتضي المشيئة والظلم بضص Deum justum esse in operibus suis, scil. versari eum in possessione sua & regno suo, ibique facere quod velit, & statuere quod libuerit, Æquitatem verò (seu justitiam) esse, cùm res loco suo collocetur, atque esse illud cum versetur quàm in regno [suo] juxta illud quod statuat voluntas, & contra autem se habere iniquitatem scil. ut sit definiente AlGazalio التصرف في ملك الغير Cùm quis versetur in dominio, seu possessione alterium, quod (inquit) محال علي الله تعالي fieri non potest ut Deo ascribatur, qui omnium dominus est.

Deo jus esse in creaturas suas, quid velit faciendi ita ut lin. 18. &c.] Eadem ferè verba apud AlSbarestanium occurrunt ubi AlAsshariensis placita recenset, وهو مالك في خلقه يفعل ما يشا ويحكم ما يريدن فلو سخل الخلائق باجمعهم الجنة لم يكن حيفا ولو ادخلهم النار لم يكن جورا ان الظلم هو التصرف فيما لا يملكه المتصرف او وضع الشي في غير موضعه وهو المالك المطلق فلا يتصور منه ظلم ولا ينسب اليه جور & c. Deus autem regnat in eo quod creavit universo, ita ut faciat quicquid velit & statuat quicquid libeat; quod si omnes simul creaturas in Paradisum intromitteret nulla in hoc foret iniquitas; vel si omnes in ignem immitteret, nulla hic esset injustitia; cum

page.notes: The Arabic lines are printed in a mixed Arabic and Latin text and are only partly legible at this scan resolution; the Arabic words are transcribed as far as they can be read, and doubtful spellings are not marked individually. The fragment "بضص" at the start of the second Arabic line before "Deum" is unclear and may be a part of a word or a printer's mark. The catchword "injustitia" stands at the right below the last line. The note "lin. 18." sits beside the line "&c.]".
